integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] 2D-animated, minimalist black line animation on a flat, digitally pure-white canvas with no texture, no gradient, no shadow, and no depth. Use minimalist two-dimensional black line animation. Show the same consistent stick figure with a hollow circular head, occasional simple line expressions, no detailed facial features, no hair, no clothing, no filled body, stable proportions, connected line limbs, and uniform medium line weight. Exactly two arms and two legs are visible per figure. Each limb appears only in its current pose: raising or lowering the right arm replaces that arm's previous line, never leaving a resting arm beneath an active arm. The figure stays black; accent colors affect only props and graphic effects. Three identical stick figures appear in this segment, all built to that same description: one enters from the left edge, one from the right edge, and one steps forward from behind the prize. A wide, static, level shot fills the 16:9 frame with empty white floor. A warm-gold rounded wine vessel with a short curved handle falls into the top of the frame and lands at the exact center of the floor with one small bounce; its outline is a smooth gold line over a solid gold fill. At the same instant the three figures step in, reach both arms toward the vessel, retract both arms together, and crouch down to the floor. An off-screen adult male narrator with a warm, clean baritone and calm, restrained delivery (S1) says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] One jar of wine. One rule.</d> while all three figures stay silent with their simple line mouths completely closed and no character dialogue occurs. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the gold vessel. [Shot 2] At 00:03.000, the shot cuts to a low, floor-level medium shot. The three crouching figures drag one fingertip each across the white floor, and three electric-blue snake lines grow outward in three directions, left, center, and right. The camera trucks right with small amplitude at slow speed as the blue lines lengthen toward the right side of the frame; the line nearest the lens passes under the lens and exits the frame. The same narrator (S1) continues in the same off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] Draw a snake on the ground. The first to finish drinks.</d> while the figures stay silent with their mouths completely closed. The three figures keep the same hollow circular heads, black line limbs, and identical proportions. [Shot 3] At 00:07.000, the shot cuts to a close-up of the electric-blue snake drawn by the center figure. Its final two strokes join head to tail; on the closing loop a single electric-blue pulse travels once around the whole outline and fades. The center figure releases the line tip with his right hand while his left hand already rises toward the gold vessel at frame right and stops just above the handle. The same narrator (S1) continues in the same off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] He finished first.</d> while all three figures stay silent with their mouths completely closed. The camera holds a static shot and pushes in very slightly on the closing loop. Throughout the segment the canvas stays flat pure white with no texture, gradient, shadow, or depth; no on-screen text, letters, numbers, captions, subtitles, signs, logos, or watermarks; no speech bubbles or dialogue boxes; no photorealistic people, faces, or 3D rendering; no extra limbs, fingers, detached hands, or additional figures beyond the three.

overall_soundscape: One low thud with a short metallic wobble as the gold vessel lands on the white floor. Bare stick feet tap the floor as the figures crouch, and three fingertips scrape lightly across the surface in thin, dry strokes. The closing electric-blue outline rings once with a clean, bright chime that decays quickly.

non_diegetic_music: Sparse single piano notes at a slow tempo over a quiet sustained ambient pad at low volume. A low piano note lands together with the vessel, and the same sparse pattern continues steadily until the end of the segment.
